There are three ways to lose an argument; you can be wrong, you can be right and lose anyway, or you can be right and win. Only the first is a mistake, the other two are structural, and treating all three as failures is how people end up refusing to enter debates at all.

The cache key is a hash of the document text and the active settings fingerprint. When either changes, the previous entry is discarded. Because the cache is bounded and keyed on content, a stale result cannot be returned for text the writer has since modified.

Rewrites are validated against the exact original substring at the recorded offsets. If the text at those offsets has changed since the preview was generated, the rewrite is rejected rather than applied, because applying it would corrupt text the writer did not agree to change.

The worker recieves a batch of chunks and returns an ordered array of decisions. Each decision is matched back to its chunk by identifier rather than by position, so a dropped response leaves an explicit hole instead of silently shifting every later chunk.

Requests carry an AbortSignal. When the writer types again, the in-flight request is aborted, and any response that arrives afterwards is discarded because its run identifier no longer matches the current one.

Analysis runs in two stages. The local engine produces issues immediately and works offline. The optional provider stage runs afterwards, only for chunks that the local engine flagged, and only when the writer has explicitly enabled it and supplied their own key.

The service worker never exposes the API key to the content script. Instead the content script sends text to the worker, the worker performs the request, and only the validated issues are returned. Each of these three steps happens in a different security context.

Offsets are mapped back to absolute document positions after chunking, and any context window added for the request is trimmed again before the response is applied. This keeps highlighted ranges aligned with the text the writer actually sees.

The response body is read through a bounded reader that refuses to buffer more than a fixed number of bytes. An oversized or malformed payload fails explicitly instead of degrading quietly, so the writer sees an error rather than an absence of suggestions.

Storage is split by responsibility. Document bodies and revision history live in IndexedDB, while small preferences live in localStorage. Neither is synchronised, and nothing is transmitted unless the writer enables a provider and supplies their own credentials.

Protected spans are identified before any rewrite is proposed. URLs, email addresses, dates, currency amounts, identifiers and quoted material are masked, so a model cannot corrupt them, and the mask is restored only if the surrounding text is unchanged.

Concurrency is capped rather than unbounded. Requests beyond the cap are queued in order, and each is cancelled when a newer edit invalidates it, so a burst of typing produces fewer requests rather than more.

The scoring model is deliberately transparent. Each dimension is derived from named signals that a reader can inspect, and no dimension is presented as a measurement. A number without a stated basis would be less honest than showing the working.
